passage: I'm Keerthana, and when I get excited telling a story, my brother Sahil holds his palms out and pushes them down gently. At first I thought it meant, “Stop, you're annoying.” Then I looked at his face. He was smiling. “Slow down, I want to hear it properly,” he said. So I took a breath and told it slowly. Yesterday my classmate did the same gesture with a stiff face and said, “Calm down.” That felt different, like she didn't want to hear me at all. Same hands, but the face and voice make it kind or not.

qa.q: What does Sahil do with his palms when Keerthana gets excited?
qa.a: He holds his palms out and pushes them down gently.

qa.q: What did Keerthana first think Sahil's gesture meant, and what changed her mind?
qa.a: She first thought it meant he found her annoying. His smile and his words, “Slow down, I want to hear it properly”, changed her mind.

qa.q: What could Keerthana do when a classmate uses the gesture with a stiff face?
qa.a: Ask calmly whether she is being too loud or say that she would like to finish her story, rather than assuming rejection.

qa.q: How might the classmate see her own gesture?
qa.a: Perhaps as a simple way to ask for calm, without noticing that her stiff face made it feel dismissive.

grounding: Palms pressing down mean slow down; kind or dismissive depends on the face and tone that come with it.

passage: Note from Raghav, sports coach. Hemant talks loudly in the huddle when he's excited. I press my palms gently downward with a smile, and he now lowers his voice. Today I saw a teammate make the same gesture with a flat face in the middle of a game. Hemant went silent and stared at his shoes. I asked him privately afterwards. He said, “It felt like he thought I was silly.” I explained that the same gesture can be kind or dismissive and that the face and tone tell you which. Next practice I will invite the two of them to talk it through.

qa.q: What does Raghav do with his palms to get Hemant to lower his voice?
qa.a: He presses his palms gently downward with a smile.

qa.q: What was Hemant feeling when he went silent after the teammate's gesture, and what else could explain it?
qa.a: Hurt and embarrassed, since he said it felt like the teammate thought he was silly. He might also have been just focusing on the game, but he told Raghav how it felt.

qa.q: What did Raghav do that helped, and what will he do next?
qa.a: He asked Hemant privately and explained that face and tone show whether the gesture is kind, and he will invite the two boys to talk it through.

qa.q: How might the teammate have meant his gesture?
qa.a: Possibly as a simple, quick request for calm in the middle of a game, without noticing his flat face looked dismissive.

grounding: Palms pressing down mean slow down; a kind or dismissive reading depends on the face and tone.

passage: Monday. Zeenat's diary. On the school bus I was telling Nikita about the puppy Abbu might bring home, and I got louder and louder. Nikita pressed both palms down in the air, slowly, like she was pushing a lid closed. I stopped. It felt like, Shut up, nobody cares. I turned to the window and sulked. Then I noticed her face: eyebrows up, eyes flicking to the front. The conductor was glaring at the back rows and had already told two boys off. Nikita whispered, “Sorry! I want to hear. Just quieter, or he'll shout.” So I whispered the rest. She squeezed my hand at the puppy's name.

qa.q: Who was glaring at the back rows?
qa.a: The conductor was glaring at the back rows.

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling when Nikita pressed her palms down?
qa.a: Zeenat felt hurt and dismissed, reading it as “shut up, nobody cares”.

qa.q: What cues helped Zeenat read the gesture differently?
qa.a: Nikita's raised eyebrows, eyes flicking to the front and whispered sorry showed worry about the conductor, not boredom.

qa.q: What was Nikita trying to say with the gesture?
qa.a: Nikita wanted to keep hearing the story and was worried the conductor would shout at them.

grounding: Shows a child reading a friend's palms-down gesture as dismissive, then using face and tone to see it was worry.

passage: The whole class was shouting about the kite festival on the temple ground, and Karthik was loudest. “Mine will go higher than the water tank!” Pallavi Teacher stood at the front and pressed both palms slowly downwards, twice. Karthik stopped. Is she cross? He checked her face. She was smiling, eyebrows relaxed, and her voice when it came was soft: “Lower, lower. I want to hear about the kites, not the whole village.” The class giggled and dropped to a murmur. Karthik raised his hand and said, in a normal voice, “Teacher, mine has a tail made from my Paati's old sari.” “Then it will fly beautifully,” she said.

qa.q: What is Karthik's kite tail made from?
qa.a: Karthik's kite tail is made from his Paati's old sari.

qa.q: What was Karthik feeling when Pallavi Teacher pressed her palms down?
qa.a: He felt a flash of worry that she was cross, until her smile and soft voice showed otherwise.

qa.q: Why did Pallavi Teacher's gesture work without upsetting anyone?
qa.a: The palms-down meant lower your voice, and pairing it with a smile, relaxed eyebrows and a soft joke made it kind, not dismissive.

qa.q: What would change if Pallavi had made the same gesture with a frown and a sharp voice?
qa.a: The class might have felt scolded and gone silent, and Karthik might not have shared his kite story.

grounding: Shows a child reading a teacher's slow-down gesture as lower your voice, with face and tone showing it was kind.

passage: In the school library in Toronto, Wei rushed over to Daniel, words tumbling out. “I got into the robotics team! They picked six from the whole grade!” Daniel, typing at the library computer, didn't turn round. He pressed one palm down twice in the air, eyes on the screen. “Calm down, it's just a club.” Wei's grin faded. The same gesture his coach used to settle the team before a match felt totally different now: no smile, no eye contact, a flat voice. Wei walked off. At lunch Daniel came over, red-faced. “Sorry about earlier. I was upset I didn't get picked. Congrats, really.”

qa.q: How many students did the robotics team pick?
qa.a: They picked six from the whole grade.

qa.q: What was Wei feeling when his grin faded?
qa.a: Wei felt hurt and brushed off, because the palm-down came with no smile, no eye contact and a flat voice.

qa.q: What did Daniel do later that helped?
qa.a: Daniel apologised, explained he was upset about not being picked and gave real congratulations.

qa.q: What was behind Daniel's gesture?
qa.a: Daniel was disappointed about not making the team himself, and it came out as a dismissive calm down.

grounding: Shows a child reading a friend's slow-down gesture as dismissive because of the face and tone that came with it.

passage:
At debate club, Yash raced through his opening speech like a train without brakes. From the back, Mr Rao smiled and pressed both palms gently down through the air. Yash took a breath and slowed. The words started to land.

Later, in the rebuttal, the other team called his idea "childish", and Yash's voice climbed. "That's not even—"

Beside him, Zainab pressed her palms down too, but her eyebrows were pinched together and she was shaking her head a little. Yash stopped. Same hands, different message: not "slower" but "careful, you're losing it". He unclenched his fist and made his point quietly. Zainab let out her breath.

qa.q: What word did the other team use for Yash's idea?
qa.a: Childish.

qa.q: What was Zainab feeling when she pressed her palms down with pinched eyebrows?
qa.a: Worried that Yash was losing his temper and might hurt their case; her shaking head backs it up, and her breath out shows relief when he calmed.

qa.q: How did Yash tell the two palm-down gestures apart?
qa.a: He read the faces that came with them: Mr Rao's smile meant "slow down", while Zainab's pinched eyebrows meant "careful, calm down".

qa.q: What would change if Mr Rao had made the gesture with an eye-roll?
qa.a: It might feel dismissive, like being told to shut up, and Yash could get flustered instead of slowing down.

grounding: It shows a child learning that the palms-down gesture means slow down from a teacher and worried calm down from a friend, read through face and tone.
